questions.q: Why does Rule 1 use `WHERE OrderTotal <= 0` instead of `WHERE OrderTotal < 0`?
options: Because a zero OrderTotal is just as invalid as a negative one for a real order, so both must be caught
Because SQL Server does not support the < operator
Because negative values are always valid at LTV Global
Because <= 0 is required syntax for every WHERE clause
questions.explain: A zero total is as much a data quality failure as a negative one for a completed order, so the rule's WHERE clause has to catch both.

questions.q: What does Rule 4, the referential integrity check, actually detect?
options: OrderLines rows whose OrderId does not exist in dbo.Orders — an orphaned row
Orders with a negative OrderTotal
Customers with a malformed email address
Duplicate SKUs in dbo.Products
questions.explain: Rule 4's NOT EXISTS clause finds OrderLines rows with no matching parent row in dbo.Orders, which is the definition of an orphaned row.

questions.q: Why does every branch of the combined UNION ALL failures report cast its key column to the same VARCHAR type?
options: Because mismatched types across UNION ALL branches raise an error or force an implicit, sometimes slow, conversion
VARCHAR is required by SQL Server for all columns
Casting has no effect on UNION ALL queries
Because OrderId and CustomerId are always the same data type by default
questions.explain: Consistent casting avoids type-mismatch errors or costly implicit conversions when combining rows of different source types via UNION ALL.

questions.q: Why does Rule 3 (SKU uniqueness) matter specifically in light of Lesson 5's glossary entry?
options: Lesson 5 defined Product as identified by a SKU that is never reused, so a duplicate SKU means that rule has already broken upstream
Lesson 5 never mentioned SKUs at all
SKU uniqueness is unrelated to any earlier lesson
Duplicate SKUs are expected and acceptable at LTV Global
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly ties Rule 3 back to Lesson 5's definition that SKUs are never reused, making a duplicate a direct violation of that glossary rule.

questions.q: According to this lesson's best practices, when should heavy data quality checks be scheduled?
options: Outside business hours, to avoid becoming an incident during peak traffic
Only during the busiest hour of the day
Checks should never be scheduled or automated
Immediately after every single transaction, in real time, with no exceptions
questions.explain: The best-practices list recommends off-peak scheduling so a full-table scan check doesn't become its own incident during checkout traffic.
